_comment: THE THREE BASELINE READINGS, RE-TAKEN, AND EVERY DIFFERENCE NAMED WITH ITS CAUSE.
The baseline is three numbers taken on 2026-09-10 and 2026-09-15: 75,971 blocks
contiguous, 138,287 objects published, and 211 of 343 historic transactions traced
across five whole 200-block windows. This is that measurement repeated on 2026-09-18,
against the same chain, over the SAME ABSOLUTE BLOCK RANGES.
The windows were originally quoted as depths below the tip. The tip was 76,024 then
and 87,114 when this ran, so a re-run by depth measures five windows eleven thousand
blocks away from the ones the baseline is over and reports the difference as a change
in the producer. The absolute range is the reproducible identity. Likewise the
backfill: this covers 1..75,971 exactly, not `genesis to tip`, because the chain has
grown and a tip-relative run is a different measurement.
-- THE OBJECT SET, AND WHAT IT IS COMPARED AGAINST ----------------------------------
`published-object-set.json` measured a tree produced on 2026-09-10 by a build whose
commit it records. That tree is gone -- it says of itself that it is machine-local --
so what can be compared is its DIGESTS, and they were computed with the generation id
in the paths. This run therefore re-ingests the merged snapshot at that same
generation id, so the comparison is about the producer rather than about a run label.
WHOLE-TREE `pathDigest` IS IDENTICAL: 138,287 objects at exactly the 138,287 paths the
record names. Seven of the ten object classes are byte-identical as well. The three
that are not are three reader changes that landed BETWEEN the two measurements, and
each is attributed to the byte by reconstruction rather than by argument -- see
`objectSet.differingClasses`, where every `reconstructedBytes` equals the recorded
`baselineBytes` exactly.
208 traced, not 211. Three transactions that replayed in the baseline refused here,
all with runtime class `unknown` -- the class the producer records when the driver's
stderr carries no thrown error at all. The cause is the HOST and it was measured, not
inferred: the replay driver is killed by SIGSEGV, exit code null, 0 bytes on stdout,
43 seconds in. See `replay.hostFinding`. Two of the three replay on a re-attempt and
one does not, which is what a crash under contention looks like from outside.
Every other figure in the replay half reproduces exactly: 343 transactions, 333
first-in-block, 5 divergent, 64 private-only, 269 with a public half, and three of the
five windows identical in every column.

contiguity._note: asserted by WALKING the ledger's 38 ranges, not by comparing a total

baseline._note: the baseline's own contiguity conclusion, recorded inside published-object-set.json's provenance; no coverage-ledger@1 artifact of it survives, so there are no pre-refactor ranges to walk

delta._note: the chain-wide population matches the committed yield artifact's chainWidePopulation exactly: 20,770 transactions, 18,508 first-in-block, 2,262 not

differingClasses.cause: two reader changes landed after the baseline tree was produced: `refusalReason` became a required member at blocktracer/chain-snapshot@2, and the outcome vocabulary was corrected from `pruned` to `not-attempted` with a longer narrative. Reconstructing the 2026-09-10 shape from these objects -- old narrative, no refusalReason -- gives 9,948,263 bytes, which is the recorded figure exactly.

four registry members landed after the baseline: identifierEncoding, reach, historyFloor and ordering. Removing exactly those four from the published row gives 538 bytes, which is the recorded figure exactly.

the `refusals` tally block landed after the baseline. Removing it gives 895 bytes, which is the recorded figure exactly. Note what did NOT move: capturedAt, tipAtCapture and finalizedAtCapture all changed VALUE between the two runs and none changed LENGTH, so the run-describing fields contribute nothing to this delta.

toolchain._hostNote: the prebuilt barretenberg native addon is renamed OFF on this host: it raises SIGILL on this CPU (no AVX2), and the WASM fallback is what makes replay possible at all.

hostFinding.what: the three transactions that moved from replayed to refused, all classified `unknown`

transactions.reAttempts: 2 of 2 refused, at 77,282 ms and 53,559 ms against a window median of 14,842 ms
2 of 2 REPLAYED, at 17,283 ms and 15,820 ms
1 refused at 43,094 ms, 1 REPLAYED at 12,194 ms

hostFinding.measurement: the driver was spawned directly against a body proxy for block 98's transaction: exit code null, signal SIGSEGV, 0 bytes on stdout, after 43,164 ms. The AVM had already simulated the transaction and printed its per-phase progress; there is no thrown error anywhere in stderr, which is exactly why the producer classifies it `unknown`.
hostFinding.conclusion: a host property, not a chain property and not a producer regression. The WASM AVM crashes on this CPU for the heaviest transactions; the same three transactions replay elsewhere in the baseline's own record.
hostFinding.residual: a row that refuses because its driver was KILLED cannot say so. `lib/replay.mjs` has the exit code and the signal in hand and neither reaches the published `reason` or `detail`; the operator sees `refused with unknown` and a progress log. Recording it would change published `reason` bytes, so it is named here rather than done inside a zero-regression measurement.
